requirements.evidence: Most of the contract exists: scoped resolution in app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:72,103,127,179; store/close resets in Queues.php:96-99,114-123; access data in Queues.php:198-213; Serve defaults/limits in app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php:38,62-69,86-103; routes at routes/web.php:57-58 and members tabs at app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:55-62. But rename passes the raw name as slug (Queues.php:129) so a rename to 'New' yields 'New', not the required 'new'; the deactivate button/label never becomes reactivate (resources/views/livewire/entity/queues.blade.php:70,119) although lang has queues_reactivate; no route-level authorization for entity.queues (routes/web.php:57); mode is unvalidated and CallMode::from can throw (Serve.php:69); serve hardcodes 'Mode' and uses ui.queues_title without :entity (serve.blade.php:15,25).

conventions.evidence: Domain writes correctly go through actions (Queues.php:85,129,153,177; Serve.php:69) and the layout/Blade style mirrors the members page. Deviations: public input properties name/renameName/mode have no #[Validate] and no $this->validate() (Queues.php:53,58; Serve.php:275) against the explicit Livewire rule; view computes data in a @php block with an inline FQCN (queues.blade.php:137-147); visible English strings bypass lang (serve.blade.php:25-30); and the TDD rule plus CHANGELOG/docs sync are not honoured (no test files and no docs in the diff).

security.evidence: Strong baseline: all client ids are resolved through $this->entity->queues()->findOrFail() / memberships()->findOrFail() (Queues.php:72,103,127,144,167,179,190,204-205,212-213) and outputs use {{ }} (queues.blade.php, serve.blade.php). Gaps: openAccess/grantAccess/revokeAccess never call $this->authorize('manageAccess', ...) and render always builds the membership list (Queues.php:160-185,198-213), so a user with Queue create but not manageAccess can see member names/emails; mode is client-writable and passed straight to CallMode::from(), causing an uncaught ValueError/500 (Serve.php:69); route-level authorization requested for employees is absent (routes/web.php:57).

tests.evidence: change.diff adds no test files at all; there are no Pest/PHPUnit tests for the new Queues/Serve components, the route protections, the tabs, or the required unauthorized-call and tamper cases (conventions.md:12-21,183-185).

simplicity.evidence: Reuses the existing layout, lang files and domain actions (Queues.php:34-36,85; Serve.php:54) with no speculative abstractions. But validation-error handling is duplicated verbatim in create() and rename() (Queues.php:57-64,121-128), the reset sequences repeat in openQueue/closeQueue (Queues.php:73-83,115-123), and the access-modal @php/grantedIds computation (queues.blade.php:137-147) adds view logic that a computed property or relation would avoid.

readability.evidence: Names and structure are clear and consistent with the members component (e.g. viewedQueue helper Queues.php:189-196, callableQueues Serve.php:42-49); methods stay small. Minor blemishes: hardcoded 'Mode'/'any'/'priority_only'/'normal_only' text in serve.blade.php:25-30, misleading labels such as revoke rendered as ui.members_cancel (queues.blade.php:151) and the queue empty state using ui.members_empty (queues.blade.php:22), plus the unused queues_reactivate string in both lang files.

scope.evidence: Every hunk serves the task: Members tab support (Members.php:55-62), two new components and views, lang keys in lang/en/ui.php:108-129 and lang/pt_BR/ui.php:108-129, navbar links (layouts/default-page.blade.php:49-56) and two routes (routes/web.php:57-58). No unrelated refactors or out-of-scope features.

issues.explanation: No Pest/PHPUnit tests were added for any new behaviour, violating the project's test-first rule and leaving the required unauthorized-call and tamper cases uncovered.

rename() passes the raw name as the slug (`slug: $this->renameName`) instead of re-deriving a slug, so renaming to 'New' produces 'New' rather than the required 'new' (and multi-word names produce invalid slugs).
The detail and confirmation buttons always render ui.queues_deactivate even when the queue is inactive; the required reactivate state is never shown and the new queues_reactivate key is unused.
The queues route is registered without route-level authorization, so the task's explicit requirement that employees get 403 at the route (not just the component mount) is not met.

`mode` is a client-writable public property with no validation and is passed straight to CallMode::from(), so a tampered value throws an uncaught ValueError and returns a 500 instead of being validated.

openAccess/grantAccess/revokeAccess do not call $this->authorize('manageAccess', $queue), and render() always loads the membership list, so authorization relies solely on SetQueueAccess and member names/emails can be disclosed to anyone who can create a queue.
Visible text is hardcoded in English ('Mode', 'any', 'priority_only', 'normal_only') and ui.queues_title is rendered without its :entity parameter, showing the literal ':entity' placeholder.
Public input properties name, renameName and mode lack #[Validate] and the actions never call $this->validate(), contrary to the project's Livewire validation convention.
The view computes granted ids in an inline @php block and references \App\Models\UserRole by FQCN, putting logic and model references in the template instead of the component.
CHANGELOG.md and the relevant docs were not updated despite the project's 'keep docs in sync' rule.
Reused generic strings are semantically wrong here: the queue empty state uses ui.members_empty, revoke is labelled ui.members_cancel, and grant is labelled ui.queues_access_button.
The ValidationException-to-field-error loop is duplicated verbatim in create() and rename() and could be extracted into one private helper.

activeTab is a plain public property, so a client can set an invalid value directly (bypassing setActiveTab's guard) and render neither tab; making the guard authoritative or hiding the raw property would be safer.

review.summary: The change adds the Queues and Serve Livewire components, their Blade views, lang keys, navbar links, routes and the members tab split, and it keeps all client ids scoped to the entity. It falls short on several required details (slug not re-derived on rename, no reactivate state, no route-level authorization, unvalidated mode) and ships no tests at all, which the project's test-first convention makes blocking; the overall verdict is that it needs changes before merging.
